PullRequest.Title: Renew marketplace resource tokens before expiry
PullRequest.Body:

Follow-up to microsoft/vscode#325804; relates to microsoft/vscode#325412.

## Summary

Renew successfully negotiated Microsoft Entra marketplace resource tokens before they expire instead of retaining the original bearer for the lifetime of the window.

- Use the existing authentication provider's `expiresAfter` lifetime in milliseconds, not JWT parsing. Resolve again at 75% of that lifetime; opaque tokens without lifetime metadata are rechecked every five minutes.
- Keep the disposable renewal scheduler in the account service, coalesce simultaneous resolutions, and reject stale results after account/provider/marketplace changes or disposal. Retry transient Unknown results after 30 seconds only when an active renewal hint was previously advertised; other providers are not newly polled, and replacing the provider or marketplace clears retry ownership.
- Retain the available manifest while renewal is pending. A thrown resource-session renewal is treated as transient only for the same previously authorized account and marketplace; a resource failure for another selected account retracts the previous bearer. Initial missing-consent/session results still follow the sign-in path.
- Publish changed authorization snapshots to the shared/remote processes without requiring a different manifest instance.
- Keep GitHub exchange behavior in microsoft/vscode#325815 unchanged. Its provider-owned refresh timer is separate; this change does not introduce a competing GitHub renewal cadence, change scopes, or replay arbitrary failed requests.

Identity-token fallback removal, redirect credential hardening, metadata caching, and forbidden-status behavior are separate focused follow-ups: microsoft/vscode#343689, microsoft/vscode#343690, microsoft/vscode#343687, and microsoft/vscode#343686 respectively.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` - passed (native TypeScript 7), including both renewal follow-ups.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` - passed.
- `npm run precommit` - passed for the four initially changed files and again for both follow-up files.
- `$env:VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH = '1'; .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\services\extensionManagement\test\electron-browser\extensionGalleryManifestService.test.ts --reporter dot` - passed, 70 tests.

Nine deterministic cases cover the precise renewal deadline, process-snapshot rotation with an unchanged catalog, retaining the manifest during renewal, opaque tokens, actual resource-acquisition failure and retry, account-switch isolation, sign-out/disposal cancellation, concurrent lookup coalescing, stale marketplace results, and preventing polling of providers without a renewal hint. Existing account, consent, origin and sign-out-race cases also pass.

A live Entra-gated deployment was not exercised. Suggested manual check: leave a signed-in window open beyond the access-token lifetime, confirm search/install/update continue without another sign-in, then sign out and confirm access is retracted. Explicit remote credential-delegation sign-off remains requested in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/343689#issuecomment-6356982275.

<sub>Drafted with GitHub Copilot.</sub>

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The recurring callback, full call path, two request-service boundaries, IPC fan-out, Extensions view listener, and default-enabled update query are all explicit in repository code. Only deployment prevalence and actual token lifetime are uncertain, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: HTTP authentication/metadata/manifest/update-query requests, IPC calls, installed-extension scans, and Extensions view rendering work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cycle repeats for the lifetime of every signed-in private-marketplace window at each refresh interval (every five minutes for the explicitly supported opaque-token case). Its update-check payload grows with installed extensions, and active-view refresh work grows with the number of visible Extensions panes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: recurring excessive network I/O and avoidable Extensions view CPU/rendering work while the window is otherwise idle
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this change, account resolution and manifest publication ran at initialization or on a real provider/account event; an unchanged signed-in window did not periodically refetch and republish its marketplace manifest.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new scheduler invokes handleAccountChange at each token deadline. The manifest service treats that as a full marketplace-account change, resolves the account, rediscovers protected-resource metadata, downloads/parses the service-index manifest, republishes it over process channels, and fires the general manifest-change event.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 505 newly schedules the account-change callback from account.refreshAfter; together with the added five-minute fallback at line 229, this converts the previously event-driven account/manifest path into recurring work even when the account and manifest are unchanged.
Findings.Title: Renew the bearer without refreshing the whole marketplace
Findings.Impact: In a long-lived Entra private-marketplace window, each renewal causes at least the protected-resource discovery and manifest HTTP work plus shared/remote IPC. If the Extensions view has been created, its manifest listener calls refresh(), which rescans local extensions, reruns visible pane searches, and—with the default extensions.autoCheckUpdates=true—issues a gallery update query for the installed-extension set. Opaque tokens repeat this burst every five minutes and can visibly refresh an open Extensions view.
Findings.Evidence: The added schedule calls the RunOnceScheduler callback handleAccountChange(). WorkbenchExtensionGalleryManifestService subscribes to onDidChangeAccount and calls handleMarketplaceAccountAccess(), whose Eligible branch calls getExtensionGalleryManifestFromServiceUrl(). MicrosoftGalleryAccountProvider.doGetAccount() also calls discoverProtectedResource(), which uses IRequestService. update() then fires onDidChangeExtensionGalleryManifest; ExtensionsViewlet's listener calls refresh(), and refresh() calls queryLocal(), doSearch(true), and checkForUpdates(). checkForUpdates() calls galleryService.getExtensions(infos, ...) and extensions.autoCheckUpdates defaults to true. The same manifest event also calls setExtensionGalleryManifest over the shared-process and optional remote channels.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep renewal on the scheduler, but give it an authorization-only path: reuse the protected-resource metadata and current manifest for the same account/service URL, update the bearer and process snapshots directly, and do not fire the general manifest-change event unless manifest capabilities actually changed. Preserve generation checks and the existing retry/cancellation semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold private-marketplace bootstrap and concurrent manifest/account lookup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Marketplace availability waits serially for the selected authentication session, protected-resource metadata discovery, resource-scoped session resolution, and the authenticated service-index manifest request. Shared/remote snapshot publication occurs after the manifest resolves and is not awaited by the caller.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the base Microsoft session and then the resource-scoped session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two session lookups for a protected resource; concurrent account callers share one sequence after this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The initial protected-marketplace bootstrap already performed both lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both lookups must complete before the authenticated manifest can be fetched.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful well-known request, or up to two attempts when a path-specific URL fails and root fallback is tried.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET and parse the private marketplace service-index manifest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for the coalesced cold bootstrap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold bootstrap already fetched the manifest once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly determines when the marketplace becomes available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish manifest and authorization to the shared process and optional remote server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per configured channel: one shared-process call and at most one remote call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Initial manifest publication already used these channels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget after manifest resolution; not on the initiating caller's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One configured marketplace and one selected account; effective cold cardinality is independent of the number of concurrent callers because of the new coalescing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The new accountRequest coalesces callers within one account generation. Authentication, discovery, resource-token resolution, and manifest download are serial. Shared-process and optional remote-channel updates are started independently and are not awaited.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: extensionGalleryManifestPromise caches the completed bootstrap; accountRequest coalesces only in-flight same-generation work. The provider stores protectedResource but does not reuse it on later resolutions. Cold bootstrap performs boundary work; warm getExtensionGalleryManifest calls return the cached manifest.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; the complete serial path and coalescing checks are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication-provider transport and network latency vary by deployment, but the serial call count is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression on cold bootstrap: expensive boundaries pre-existed, while the diff reduces duplicate concurrent account resolutions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Successful scheduled token renewal in a long-lived window, including an instantiated Extensions view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The timer is off the user's initiating critical path, but authorization publication waits for account resolution, metadata discovery, resource-token resolution, and a fresh manifest download. The resulting general manifest event then starts process publication and Extensions view refresh work; an active Extensions view can visibly refresh while in use.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-resolve the base and resource-scoped Microsoft sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two lookups per renewal cycle, coalesced across simultaneous account callers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Without a provider/account event, an idle window did not periodically perform these lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the renewed bearer is published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rediscover protected-resource metadata even though protectedResource is retained on the provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful request or up to two well-known URL attempts per renewal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Discovery occurred on initialization or actual account events, not on a timer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Redownload and parse the service-index manifest after token renewal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An unchanged idle account did not trigger recurring manifest downloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new bearer is not installed/published until this request completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Republish the full manifest and new authorization snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared-process call plus at most one remote-server call per renewal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Process publication occurred only with bootstrap or an actual manifest/account update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the account-resolution critical path but part of each renewal fan-out.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-query installed extensions from local, remote, and web extension-management servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one sequential query per available server whenever the Extensions view listener handles the manifest event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No periodic token timer fired the manifest listener.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the rest of ExtensionsViewlet.refresh and can affect an open Extensions UI.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check installed extensions against the gallery through galleryService.getExtensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched gallery request containing the effective installed-extension set when extensions.autoCheckUpdates is enabled (default true).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A token deadline did not trigger an update check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Started after the installed-extension scan; it can overlap visible-pane queries and is not needed to rotate the bearer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-run each Extensions pane query and replace its list model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per instantiated pane; gallery-backed panes can each issue a gallery query, while local panes rescan/filter installed state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These pane refreshes were tied to actual manifest changes, not idle token deadlines.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can visibly refresh the active Extensions view and consume network/renderer work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Window lifetime divided by token refresh interval; installed-extension count controls the update-check payload, and instantiated/visible Extensions panes control query and render fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One RunOnceScheduler deadline is active, and accountRequest coalesces same-generation callers. Discovery, token resolution, and manifest download are serial. After publication, one or two IPC calls are fire-and-forget; ExtensionsViewlet first awaits sequential local/remote/web installed-extension queries, then starts visible-pane searches and the update check without awaiting either, so those requests can overlap.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Only concurrent account calls are coalesced. Warm renewals do not reuse the stored protected-resource metadata or current manifest, and the general manifest event bypasses the Extensions view's existing query result by invoking show again. Opaque tokens explicitly schedule this path every five minutes; expiring tokens use 75% of their lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high; scheduler callback, serial network path, manifest event, default configuration, and downstream listeners are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Private-marketplace adoption, token lifetimes, number of installed extensions, and whether the Extensions view has been instantiated vary. The opaque-token five-minute cadence and default-enabled update check establish a realistic recurring trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: a bearer renewal is routed through full manifest reload/publication and unrelated Extensions UI/update work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Transient resource-token renewal failure and 30-second retry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A failed resource-session lookup leaves the available manifest in place, so marketplace reads can continue with the prior snapshot. The retry timer is off the immediate user critical path; a successful later retry follows the full renewal path before rotating authorization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the base session and attempt the resource-scoped session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two lookups on each retry attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no timer-owned renewal retry loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The failed attempt does not block use of the retained manifest, but each retry waits on these operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rediscover protected-resource metadata before each resource-session retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful discovery or up to two fallback attempts every 30 seconds while the transient Unknown state persists and retryRenewal remains owned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Transient idle-window retries did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serial prerequisite for each retry, though off current marketplace availability's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the manifest after the resource session eventually succeeds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on a failed resource-session attempt; one on the first successful retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No scheduled retry reached this manifest request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before successful authorization rotation is published.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Duration of the authentication-provider outage divided by 30 seconds; effective concurrency remains one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: There is one RunOnceScheduler retry and one coalesced account request per generation. Failures do not accumulate concurrent retries; provider/account changes and disposal cancel ownership through generation changes and scheduler disposal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The current manifest and bearer remain available through Unknown failures. There is no negative cache for metadata or resource-session failures; retry is time-bounded at 30 seconds and stops when retry ownership is cleared.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; state transition, retry guard, scheduler, and retained-manifest branch are covered directly by code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Outage duration is unknown. The retry interval and lack of concurrent accumulation are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the retry is bounded and preserves availability; its redundant discovery is part of the already reported renewal fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Account/provider/service replacement, sign-out, stale completion, and disposal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Real account/session changes intentionally trigger one fresh account/manifest resolution. Sign-out resolves the base session then retracts authorization without protected-resource or manifest requests. Stale in-flight results are rejected before publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve session state after a real account/provider event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced resolution for the new generation; sign-out ends after this lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Actual account changes already required account resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines when sign-out/account-switch state is published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover metadata for an eligible replacement account/service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one discovery sequence for the surviving generation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Eligible account changes already rediscovered access metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required only for eligible protected-resource access.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the authenticated manifest for the surviving eligible generation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request; canceled/stale resolution tokens suppress publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Account changes already refetched the manifest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before making the replacement account's marketplace available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of actual account/provider changes, not collection size or window lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: handleAccountChange cancels the scheduled deadline, increments the generation, and clears the coalesced request. Service-URL changes do the same. RunOnceScheduler is registered for disposal. A previously started boundary call may finish, but generation/cancellation checks prevent it from scheduling or publishing stale state.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: In-flight work is coalesced only within a generation. Provider/account/service replacement invalidates it; disposal cancels the scheduler. No retained timer or unbounded map remains after disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; generation checks, cancellation source, scheduler cancellation, and disposal ownership are explicit and tested.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: An underlying request may not abort immediately depending on transport, but stale results are bounded to already-started work and cannot recursively reschedule.
Scenarios.Verdict: No cleanup/concurrency finding: cancellation and generation ownership bound stale work and prevent timer leaks or bursts.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and traced bootstrap, renewal, retry, UI/process propagation, replacement, and disposal paths. Submitted one medium-confidence-impact finding for the high-confidence recurring boundary fan-out from token renewal into metadata/manifest reloads, IPC, extension scans, gallery update checks, and view refreshes. Coalescing, stale-result rejection, retry serialization, and cleanup are otherwise bounded.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
